task_0075.solver_message:
Some spheres still out of frustum at z=12. Let me compute required camera distance for fov=30 to cover the horizontal extent (-5.1 to 5.1, half-width 5.1) plus margin.

Half-width 5.5 with margin → dist = 5.5 / tan(15°) ≈ 20.5. But h-fov also depends on aspect ratio (typically 16:9 in editor default 1152x648 project → narrower). Let me just test z=22 and also slightly reduce margins. Also vertical extent: y -1.1 to 1, camera at y=1 → vertical range [-2.1, 0], half ~1.05 — well within v-fov (30° vertical? In Godot, fov is vertical FOV... actually Godot's Camera3D fov is vertical). Wait — if fov is vertical = 30°, then tan(15°) covers vertical half. Vertical needed: from y=1 down to -1.1 = 2.1 → dist = 2.1/tan(15°) ≈ 7.8. Horizontal: with aspect 16:9, h_half_angle = atan(tan(15°)*16/9) = atan(0.476) ≈ 25.4°, tan ≈ 0.476. dist = 5.5/0.476 ≈ 11.5. Hmm, then z=12 should nearly work. The in_frustum=false for sphere at x=3.8: dist 12, h offset 3.8/12 = 0.3167 < 0.476 → should be in frustum... Wait, camera is at z=12, sphere at z=3.2 → effective distance 12-3.2 = 8.8. x=3.8 → 3.8/8.8=0.432 < 0.476 OK barely. Sphere3 x=4.6, z=-0.6 → dist 12.6, 4.6/12.6=0.365 OK. Hmm but it says false. Maybe the frustum check ran before viewport update? Or the default viewport aspect in headless is 1:1 — then h half-width at dist 12.6 = tan(15°)*12.6 = 3.38 < 4.6. Yes, that's it.

Headless default window is small. Rather than relying on rendering viewport, push camera back to z=18 and also shift camera look slightly. Let's compute worst: sphere4 x=-4.2, radius 0.5 → need h offset 4.7 visible. If aspect 1:1: dist needed = 4.7/tan(15°) ≈ 17.5. Sphere4 z=1.7 → camera z = 1.7+17.5 = 19.2. Use z=20 for margin. Vertical: sphere below: y -1.1, from cam y=1 → 2.1 below; at dist 20 works.

Let's try z=20.
